nodes.summary: For every tree model over a finite set of values, the belief of the root, vertex $0$, is the root message computed by variable elimination: the two agree at every value.
nodes.title: Belief at the root is the root message

nodes.summary: The belief of each vertex of a tree model over a finite set of values, computed by sum-product message passing: the product of its unary factor, the messages from its subtree and the message from its parent. Recursively, in a model with a single vertex the belief of that vertex is its unary factor; in a model with vertices $0, \dots, n + 1$ the belief of the last vertex at a value $b$ is its unary factor at $b$…
nodes.title: Sum-product belief

nodes.summary: An assignment of a tree model over a finite nonempty set of values, defined by recursion on the number of vertices. For a single vertex, its value is one that maximizes its unary factor. For vertices $0, \dots, n + 1$, the vertices $0, \dots, n$ get the decoding of the model with the last vertex maximized out, and the last vertex gets a value $b$ maximizing $\psi(b, a)\, \phi(b)$, where $a$ is the decoded value of…
nodes.title: Max-product decoding

nodes.summary: For a tree model with vertices $0, \dots, n + 1$ over a finite set of values, the message from the parent $p$ of the last vertex to the last vertex at a value $b$ is the sum over all values $a$ of $\psi(b, a)\, \beta(a)$, where $\psi$ is the factor of the edge between the last vertex and $p$ (last vertex first) and $\beta(a)$ is the belief of $p$ at $a$ in the model without the last vertex.
nodes.title: Downward message to the last vertex

nodes.summary: For a tree model with vertices $0, \dots, n + 1$, the tree model on $0, \dots, n$ with the same parents, unary factors and edge factors: the last vertex, which is a leaf, is removed together with its unary factor and the factor of its edge.
nodes.title: Removing the last vertex

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be finite, let $m$ be a pairwise tree model on the vertices $0, \dots, n + 1$ with parents $p$, unary factors $\varphi_i$ and pairwise factors $\psi_k$, and let $\mu$ be the message from the last vertex $n + 1$ to its parent $q = p(n + 1)$. Eliminating the last vertex gives the pairwise tree model on the vertices $0, \dots, n$ in which vertex $k + 1$ has parent $p(k + 1)$ and edge factor $\psi_k$ for…
nodes.title: Eliminating the last vertex of a tree model

nodes.summary: In a pairwise tree model on the vertices $0, \dots, n + 1$, this is the parent of the last vertex $n + 1$, regarded as one of the vertices $0, \dots, n$ of the tree with the last vertex removed.
nodes.title: Parent of the last vertex

nodes.summary: For every tree model over a finite set of values, every vertex $v$ and every value $a$, the belief of $v$ at $a$ is the unnormalized marginal of $v$ at $a$: the sum of the weights of all assignments $x$ with $x_v = a$.
nodes.title: Beliefs are the unnormalized marginals

nodes.summary: For a tree model with vertices $0, \dots, n + 1$ over a finite nonempty set of values, the tree model on $0, \dots, n$ with the same parents and edge factors whose unary factor at the parent of the last vertex is multiplied by the max-product message of the last vertex; the other unary factors are unchanged.
nodes.title: Maximizing out the last vertex

nodes.summary: For a tree model with vertices $0, \dots, n + 1$ over a finite nonempty set of values, the max-product message from the last vertex to its parent at a value $a$ is the maximum over all values $b$ of $\psi(b, a)\, \phi(b)$, where $\psi$ is the factor of the edge between the last vertex and its parent and $\phi$ is the unary factor of the last vertex.
nodes.title: Max-product message

nodes.summary: For a tree model over a finite nonempty set of values, the value computed by maximizing out the vertices from the last one down: for a single vertex it is the maximum of its unary factor over all values, and for more vertices it is the max-product value of the model with the last vertex maximized out.
nodes.title: Max-product value

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be finite and consider a pairwise tree model on the vertices $0, \dots, n + 1$ with unary factors $\varphi_i$ and pairwise factors $\psi_k$. The message from the last vertex $n + 1$ to its parent is the function $\mu : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ given by $\mu(a) = \sum_{b \in \alpha} \psi_n(b, a) \, \varphi_{n+1}(b)$, where $\psi_n$ is the factor of the edge between vertex $n + 1$ and its parent.
nodes.title: Message from the last vertex

nodes.summary: A tree model has nonnegative factors when all its unary factors and all its edge factors take only nonnegative values.
nodes.title: Nonnegative factors

nodes.summary: In a pairwise tree model on the vertices $0, \dots, n$, for $k < n$ the parent of vertex $k + 1$ is the parent recorded by the model, an element of $\{0, \dots, k\}$, regarded as one of the vertices $0, \dots, n$.
nodes.title: Parent of a vertex

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be finite and let $m$ be a pairwise tree model on the vertices $0, \dots, n$ with weight $w$ and root message $r : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$. Then the partition function of $m$ is the total root message: $\sum_x w(x) = \sum_{a \in \alpha} r(a)$, where $x$ ranges over all assignments $\{0, \dots, n\} \to \alpha$.
nodes.title: Variable elimination computes the partition function

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be finite and let $m$ be a pairwise tree model on the vertices $0, \dots, n$ with weight $w$ and root message $r : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$. Then for every $a \in \alpha$ the unnormalized marginal of the root at $a$ equals $r(a)$, that is, $\sum_x w(x) = r(a)$, where $x$ ranges over the assignments $\{0, \dots, n\} \to \alpha$ with $x_0 = a$.
nodes.title: Variable elimination computes the unnormalized root marginal

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be finite. The root message of a pairwise tree model $m$ on the vertices $0, \dots, n$ is the function $r_m : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ defined by recursion on $n$: if $n = 0$, it is the unary factor of the root $0$; if $m$ is a model on the vertices $0, \dots, n + 1$, it is $r_{m'}$, where $m'$ is the model on the vertices $0, \dots, n$ obtained from $m$ by eliminating the last vertex.
nodes.title: Root message of a tree model

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a pairwise tree model on the vertices $0, \dots, n + 1$ with values in a finite type $\alpha$, and let $m'$ be the model on the vertices $0, \dots, n$ obtained from $m$ by summing out its last vertex. Write $w_m$ and $w_{m'}$ for their unnormalized weights. Then for every vertex $v \le n$ and every function $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$,
nodes.title: Summing out the last vertex preserves weighted sums at the other vertices

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be finite, let $m$ be a pairwise tree model on the vertices $0, \dots, n + 1$ with weight $w$, and let $m'$ be the model on the vertices $0, \dots, n$ obtained from $m$ by eliminating the last vertex, with weight $w'$. Then for every function $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ we have $\sum_x w(x) \, g(x_0) = \sum_y w'(y) \, g(y_0)$, where $x$ ranges over all assignments $\{0, \dots, n + 1\} \to \alpha$ and…
nodes.title: One step of variable elimination

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a pairwise tree model on the vertices $0, \dots, n$ with values in a finite type $\alpha$, let $w$ be its unnormalized weight, and let $b_v$ be the belief of vertex $v$ computed by sum-product message passing. Then for every vertex $v$ and every function $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$,
nodes.title: Belief propagation is exact on trees

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be finite and let $m$ be a pairwise tree model on the vertices $0, \dots, n$ with weight $w$ and root message $r : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$. Then for every function $g : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ of the root value, $\sum_x w(x) \, g(x_0) = \sum_{a \in \alpha} r(a) \, g(a)$, where $x$ ranges over all assignments $\{0, \dots, n\} \to \alpha$.
nodes.title: Variable elimination is exact

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ of values and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, a pairwise tree model on the vertices $0, \dots, n$ consists of a parent $p(k + 1) \in \{0, \dots, k\}$ for each vertex $k + 1$ with $k < n$ (so vertex $0$ is the root and every vertex comes after its parent), a unary factor $\varphi_i : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ for each vertex $i \le n$, and for each $k < n$ a pairwise factor $\psi_k(a, b) \in \mathbb{R}$ on the…
nodes.title: Pairwise model on a tree

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a pairwise tree model with values in a finite nonempty type, and let $M$ be its max-product value, obtained by maximizing out the vertices from the last one down. Then the weight of the assignment produced by max-product decoding equals $M$.
nodes.title: Max-product decoding attains the max-product value

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a pairwise tree model with values in a finite nonempty type $\alpha$ whose unary and pairwise factors are all nonnegative, and let $M$ be its max-product value, obtained by maximizing out the vertices from the last one down. Then every assignment of values in $\alpha$ to the vertices has weight at most $M$.
nodes.title: The max-product value bounds every weight

nodes.summary: Let $m$ be a pairwise tree model with values in a finite nonempty type $\alpha$ whose unary and pairwise factors are all nonnegative. Then every assignment of values in $\alpha$ to the vertices has weight at most the weight of the assignment produced by max-product decoding.
nodes.title: Max-product decoding finds a MAP assignment

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type and let $m$ be a pairwise model on a tree with vertices $0, \dots, n$, with unary factors $\varphi_i : \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ for each vertex $i$, and with factor $\psi_k : \alpha \times \alpha \to \mathbb{R}$ on the edge between vertex $k + 1$ and its parent $p(k + 1)$ for each $k < n$. The unnormalized weight of an assignment $x : \{0, \dots, n\} \to \alpha$ is the real number
nodes.title: Weight of an assignment in a tree model

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
